investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-08T01:05–01:06Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api gateway could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because the failure is upstream of agent provisioning, no evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected and all contract assertions are unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service that backs POST /api/agents → http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check depends on this single upstream call to create an agent before any further state or runtime probing can occur. The 502 response with code "bad_gateway" and the identical error message across all three sibling checks (evidenced by failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-state, sibling.remote-agent-runtime) confirms the failure is at the shared swarm gateway layer, not in any individual check's logic. This is an eval-detected infrastructure availability issue; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact to production end-users cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

possibleCauses: Most likely — Swarm ELB endpoint (us-east-2) is down, misconfigured, or has no healthy targets: the 502 bad_gateway with a connection-send error to the ELB URL is the direct signal. All three checks share this dependency and all returned the same error within the same minute.

Transient network partition or DNS resolution failure between the production-api service and the swarm ELB in us-east-2: the ~11-second latency before the 502 is consistent with a TCP connection attempt that was refused or reset rather than a DNS NXDOMAIN (which would be near-instant).

Swarm service deployment or restart in progress at the time of the eval run: a rolling restart or failed deployment could cause the ELB to report no healthy targets, producing a 502 from the load balancer itself.
ELB security group or VPC routing change blocking inbound traffic from the production-api caller: would produce the same 502 symptom without the swarm service itself being down.

Eval infrastructure credential or endpoint misconfiguration causing the wrong ELB URL to be targeted: less likely given the error message contains a real ELB hostname and the failure is consistent across three independent check invocations.

Add an eval that validates the GitHub Pages deployment status for the observability/status.json artifact independently of the snapshot content, catching deployment failures that leave a stale artifact even when the generation workflow succeeds.

Add a historical trend eval that tracks snapshotAgeMinutes across consecutive runs to detect gradual drift (e.g., a workflow running but increasingly delayed) before it crosses the hard contract boundary.
